active_paradigms.idea: Use the known optimal 14-point Tammes/anti-podal configuration from the 'maximal minimum distance' literature as an analytic seed, then apply exact semidefinite-style gradient flow on the squared ratio
active_paradigms.description: The problem of maximizing dmin/dmax for 14 points in 3D is closely related to the Tammes problem (N=14 on a sphere) and known best configurations exist in the literature (e.g., Musin-Tarasov-type arrangements, heptagonal double rings, and the 14-vertex rhombic dodecahedron variants). Hard-code several candidate optimal 14-point point sets as exact numeric seeds (double heptagonal rings with twist angles, the icosahedron+2 poles, and the rhombic dodecahedron vertices) computed to full double precision, then run a single direct optimization of the squared ratio objective f = (dmin/dmax)^2 using its exact subgradient: move the two points realizing dmin apart and the two realizing dmax together, with step sizes from a Barzilai-Borwein schedule. Unlike the homotopy/bisection approach, this directly climbs the true objective with a well-defined subgradient direction, avoiding the feasibility-restoration overhead that wastes budget. The key breakthrough is that the current program spends most time on bisection solves; a direct ratio ascent from a near-optimal analytic seed converges to the local optimum in a few hundred iterations.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score by starting essentially at the optimum and polishing with exact subgradient ascent on (dmin/dmax)^2
active_paradigms.cautions: The ratio objective is non-smooth at ties; use a softmin/softmax over pairwise distances with a temperature that decreases over iterations to keep gradients well-defined and to handle multiple shortest/longest pairs. Normalize diameter to 1 periodically. Keep the analytic seeds in unit-diameter normalization so the reference benchmark 1/4.165849767 is directly comparable.

active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-restricted parametric search: optimize only the free parameters of symmetric point-set families (rings, twisted antiprisms, poles) with dense multistart on a low-dimensional parameter space
active_paradigms.description: Instead of optimizing 42 free coordinates, hypothesize that the optimum has symmetry. Candidate families: (1) two staggered regular heptagons (7+7) at heights ±h with relative twist angle θ and radii r1, r2; (2) one regular hexagon ring + hexagon cap + 2 poles; (3) antiprism-based arrangements. Each family has only 2-5 free parameters, so the ratio can be maximized by a dense grid search followed by a fine local refinement (e.g., scipy.optimize.minimize with Nelder-Mead on the 3-5 parameters, which is a direct problem solve, not hyperparameter tuning). Evaluate thousands of parameter combinations cheaply since each evaluation is O(n^2) closed-form. The best family output is then used directly. This differs fundamentally from the current approach because it exploits symmetry to reduce dimensionality, guaranteeing the search finds the symmetric local optimum exactly rather than hoping a 42-dimensional homotopy lands there.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score via exhaustive coverage of low-dimensional symmetric families, ensuring the globally best symmetric configuration is found to machine precision
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not assume the global optimum is symmetric; run all families plus a few asymmetric perturbation checks. The heptagonal double ring (7+7 antiprism-like) is a strong candidate for N=14 since 14 = 2×7. Compute the ratio in closed form from ring geometry to make grid search fast. Use Nelder-Mead (derivative-free) since the ratio is non-smooth in the parameters.

active_paradigms.idea: Max-min distance via convex-geometry: iterated farthest-point insertion with local Delaunay/Voronoi repair using scipy.spatial
active_paradigms.description: Use scipy.spatial.Voronoi and ConvexHull to implement a construction heuristic: start from a candidate set, then repeatedly (a) identify the shortest edge in the Delaunay triangulation (scipy.spatial.Delaunay), (b) move one of its endpoints toward the centroid of its farthest Voronoi neighbor cell, and (c) shrink the diameter by projecting extreme hull vertices (scipy.spatial.ConvexHull vertices) inward along their hull normals. This is a geometric repair loop rather than a generic NLP: shortest edges are fixed by pushing points toward underpopulated Voronoi regions, longest edges (diameter pairs) are fixed by contracting hull extremes. Alternate these two repairs with decreasing step size. Because each step uses exact geometric structure (Delaunay neighbors, hull facets), it makes targeted, globally-informed moves that random hill-climbing cannot, and it uses scipy.spatial which has not been tried in the failed attempts (only scipy.optimize and spectral graph methods failed).
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score by geometrically targeted repair of the shortest and longest distance pairs
active_paradigms.cautions: Delaunay triangulation can be degenerate for near-cocircular points; wrap in try/except and fall back to nearest-neighbor moves. Ensure the point set stays non-degenerate (no coincident points) before each triangulation. Track the true ratio after each repair and keep the best configuration seen, since repairs are heuristic and may temporarily worsen the ratio.

tried_paradigms.idea: Optimize the squared-distance feasibility problem directly with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') using nonlinear constraints d(i,j)^2 >= t and d(i,j)^2 <= 1, maximizing t as an extra variable.
tried_paradigms.description: Reformulate exactly as the evaluator hints: variables are the 42 point coordinates plus t; constraints are 91 lower bounds d^2 - t >= 0 and 91 upper bounds 1 - d^2 >= 0, all smooth quadratics with analytic Jacobians. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr', minimizing -t, supplying NonlinearConstraint objects with vectorized constraint functions and precomputed sparse Jacobians (each constraint involves only 6 coordinates). Warm-start from the current best configuration (which already achieves ratio ~0.4898) and from structured seeds. Because trust-constr handles the KKT conditions of the true feasibility NLP, it can push t past what penalty-based L-BFGS homotopy reaches, since penalty methods leave a small feasibility gap. Increase t incrementally (t += 1e-5) re-solving each time, an exact feasible ascent on the certified lower bound. Guard with time checks and return the best feasible configuration normalized to unit diameter.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / benchmark; directly maximizes the certified lower bound t
tried_paradigms.cautions: Provide analytic Jacobians (2*(xi-xj) pattern) and use sparse LinearConstraint-style sparsity via NonlinearConstraint with jac returning sparse matrices for speed; verify final feasibility numerically (all distances in [t,1]-1e-9) before returning; keep total runtime under the timeout by limiting major iterations per t-step.

tried_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping on the exact ratio objective using scipy.optimize.basinhopping with a min-max aware step generator.
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping on the objective f(p) = -(dmin/dmax) with a custom take_step that moves the point participating in the currently shortest or longest edge along the pair direction (the gradient-informative directions), plus occasional random rotations of the whole configuration (invariance-aware moves that don't change the objective but help escape basins when combined with perturbation). Each basin-hopping iteration locally minimizes with L-BFGS-B on a smooth surrogate: maximize sum of softmin distances, e.g. objective -logsumexp(-d/eps) combined with diameter penalty, which approximates the true nonsmooth ratio well for small eps. Run multiple seeds including the known good structured seeds (icosahedron+2 poles, double hexagon rings). The key difference from the current hill-climb is acceptance of worsening moves (Metropolis) enabling escape from the local optimum at ratio ~0.4898.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary (dmin/dmax)^2 via the smooth surrogate and exact ratio evaluation at the end
tried_paradigms.cautions: The true ratio is nonsmooth; always do final local polish on the exact ratio; set temperature adaptively (accept ~20-30%); use fixed seed; enforce time budget by capping niter based on elapsed time per iteration.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exploit graph/geometric structure: parameterize candidate 14-point configurations by distance-graph topology and search over contact graphs with a force-balance (Stress majorization / spectral) solver.
tried_paradigms.description: At the optimum, the shortest and longest distances form contact graphs. Enumerate plausible topologies: e.g., 14 vertices as two staggered hexagonal rings plus 2 poles (best known candidates), or icosahedron-based capsid structures. For a hypothesized graph with prescribed edge lengths all equal to 1 (both min and max contacts at 1), solve the graph realization / stress equilibrium: find coordinates where each vertex is in equilibrium under unit forces along its contact edges (a first-order condition of the optimum). Implement as fixed-point iteration: each point moves to the weighted centroid of its graph neighbors (stress majorization à la scipy-free implementation, or use scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs on the stress matrix). Then verify and hill-climb. Additionally try spectral placement: use the eigenvectors of the contact-graph Laplacian as initial 3D embedding, then refine. This explores fundamentally different geometric structures than random repulsion seeds.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score by discovering a better contact topology than the current best local optimum
tried_paradigms.cautions: Graph realization may not exist for a hypothesized topology; check all pairwise distances and discard infeasible realizations; keep several topologies within time budget; use fixed seeds for any randomized refinement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Add unexplored symmetric polyhedral seed families: heptagonal antiprism (14 vertices, all-equal edges), heptagonal prism, gyroelongated structures, and the 14-vertex rhombic dodecahedron variants, then homotopy-refine them
tried_paradigms.description: The current program's graph seeds are limited to 6+6+2 rings, icosahedron+caps, cuboctahedron+caps, and one rhombic dodecahedron wiring. A heptagonal antiprism has exactly 14 vertices, is vertex-transitive with two edge classes (side edges and top/bottom heptagon edges) — by tuning the heptagon radius r and height h you can make side edges and heptagon edges both approach the diameter/equality conditions, giving a natural 2-parameter family to sweep (e.g., 20x20 grid over r in [0.5,1.5], h in [0.2,1.5]). Similarly add the heptagonal prism (14 vertices), the gyroelongated pentagonal bipyramid family, and the 14-vertex Johnson-solids. Critically, after picking each (r,h) analytically compute dmin and dmax and only homotopy-refine the top-k grid entries — this avoids wasting budget on bad parameterizations. Feed these seeds through the existing homotopy solver but with the improved initial t set to the analytic ratio, so bisection starts tight. This directly explores topologies the current program never touches, and the known best solutions for the related n=14 diameter-constrained packing often have antiprism-like local structure.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score (dmin/dmax)^2 via structurally new candidate optima
tried_paradigms.cautions: Sweep the parameter grid cheaply with pure numpy distance computations before invoking L-BFGS; ensure the antiprism is built with exact vertex coordinates (r*cos(2*pi*k/7 + phase), r*sin(...), ±h/2) with the 7-fold twist of pi/7 for the antiprism; keep the wall-clock budget guard; normalize each seed to unit diameter before homotopy.

tried_paradigms.idea: Directly solve the constrained NLP 'maximize t subject to d(i,j)^2 >= t, d(i,j)^2 <= 1' with scipy.optimize.minimize using method='trust-constr' and analytic Jacobian constraint matrices
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator's own reformulation suggests the natural formulation: variables are the 42 point coordinates plus t, maximize t (minimize -t) with 91 lower-bound and 91 upper-bound nonlinear pairwise-distance constraints. Unlike the current penalty homotopy, trust-constr handles these constraints natively with the interior-point/SQP filter method, staying on the feasible manifold and giving KKT-quality stationary points. Compute the constraint Jacobians analytically: for constraint g_ij = d(i,j)^2 - t >= 0, d/dx_i = 2(x_i - x_j), d/dt = -1; similarly for the upper bounds. Add tiny regularization or a symmetry anchor (fix first point at origin, second on x-axis, third in xy-plane) to remove the 6 rigid-motion degrees of freedom, which dramatically improves conditioning. Run this from the top ~10 seeds found by the existing seeding code (this is deterministic setup, one optimization per seed), then take the best t. This converges to exact local optima of the true problem rather than approximate penalty minimizers, which typically leaves 1e-4 to 1e-3 of ratio on the table.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score by finding exact KKT points of the true constrained problem
tried_paradigms.cautions: Scaling matters: work with squared distances and normalize so coordinates are O(1); set gtol=1e-12, xtol=1e-14; provide both constraints as a single vector-valued function with a dense 182x43 Jacobian; the rigid-motion anchoring must be consistent (not all points collinear); fall back to SLSQP if trust-constr stalls; keep total runtime under the budget by limiting to ~10 starts with maxiter=2000.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace bisection homotopy with a smooth annealed surrogate: optimize the differentiable log-sum-exp softmin/softmax of squared distances with L-BFGS, sharpening the temperature schedule to recover the exact ratio
tried_paradigms.description: The exact ratio dmin/dmax is non-smooth (argmin/argmax switching), which is why the current hill-climb and penalty approach struggle near the optimum. Define a smooth surrogate S_beta(p) = -logsumexp(-beta * d^2)/beta divided by logsumexp(beta * d^2)/beta (a smooth lower/upper approximation of min and max of squared distances). For moderate beta this is fully differentiable with a closed-form gradient (softmax weights over pairs), so scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' and jac=True can optimize it robustly. Start at beta ~ 2 (very smooth landscape, no local-minimum switching) and anneal beta upward (x2 each stage, up to ~500), warm-starting each stage from the previous solution; as beta grows the surrogate converges monotonically to the true ratio, and the smooth early stages guide the optimizer across the non-smooth kinks that trap the current code. Run this annealing chain from each of the top graph seeds and generic seeds; finish with a few exact-ratio polish steps. Because the surrogate gradient distributes weight over ALL near-minimal and near-maximal pairs simultaneously, it naturally resolves the degenerate contact graphs where multiple pairs tie at dmin and dmax — exactly the structure of the optimum.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score by smoothing the non-smooth min/max objective to escape kink-induced local optima
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use scipy.special.logsumexp with beta-scaled inputs to avoid overflow; normalize points to unit diameter at each annealing stage to keep scale fixed (the surrogate is scale-sensitive); gradient uses softmax weights w_ij = exp(beta*(c - d_ij^2)) over the 91 pairs — assemble via np.add.at like the existing penalty gradient; choose per-stage convergence ftol=1e-16 so stages fully converge before sharpening; guard total time; verify the final exact ratio after annealing and keep the best over all chains.
